# V15 Amin: retained local income did not preserve the win

All24 fixed family games finished before this final interpretation (Amin1768 exit0, external49500 exit0 reported by root). This report covers the eight complete Amin histories: four policies on one consumed placement with two seat/spawn-label mirrors. It is not independent fresh strength evidence or a full-family ranking.

| Policy | Both mirrored outcomes | Terminal turn | Frontier overrides per game |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| V10 | 2 wins |1033|0|
| V10-v6 |2 losses|370|0|
| V15 tick |2 losses|239|2|
| V15 fanout |2 losses|369|23|

Neither V15 mode preserves the best retained control's win on Amin. V10-v6 is weaker on this placement. No promotion or superiority claim follows.

## The intended frontier behavior actually executed

Tick mode changes only49 and99. At49 it sends half of home6 NORTH into empty(7,17), leaving reserve3; the captured tile has4 at observation50. It replaces a7-army transfer(14,16)→owned(15,16). At99 it sends half of3 from(15,11) WEST into empty(15,10); that tile has2 at100. Both captures survive continuously through their next land tick. The first remains owned through the last preterminal observation; the second is lost at129.

Fanout changes23 actions between16 and110. Every override captures its destination in the next original observation. Twenty-two remain continuously owned through their next land tick; the(15,12) capture at106 is lost131 and later recaptured, so it is not credited with continuous retention. Two initial captures16/17 expand north from home; subsequent choices spread distributed small garrisons.

These gains are not free action slots. At50–52 fanout displaces the same parent proposal to move the8-army packet from(14,17) west. At100–107 it displaces the same9-army packet's transfer from(13,17) south on eight consecutive decisions. The chosen little captures are real, but they repeatedly defer transport of the larger parent packet. The records do not establish that this delay alone caused the eventual loss.

First candidate raw divergence versus V10 is49 for tick and16 for fanout; first opponent raw divergence is129 for both. Neither public history plus underlying19-field parent memory subsequently rejoins V10 before its termination. There is no isolated single-intervention counterfactual identifying one override as sufficient cause.

## Production, contact and exposure

Cells below are **our land/army : opponent land/army; exact retained plain1→2 count** on the actual tick transition. The1→2 count is an observed cell transition, distinct from total territory income and from newly captured larger stacks.

|Turn|V10|V10-v6|V15 tick|V15 fanout|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|50|14/40 :19/45;11|same|15/41 :19/45;12|15/41 :19/45;12|
|100|43/108 :41/111;38|same|44/110 :41/111;38|43/109 :41/111;35|
|150|64/191 :55/185;45|72/198 :54/183;48|68/193 :51/177;47|60/186 :53/181;47|
|200|75/228 :70/217;36|70/228 :71/214;13|77/245 :64/216;24|65/192 :58/180;21|

Tick shows real additional land/income yet dies sooner. Fanout has no land advantage at100 despite twelve overrides before that observation. Reserve compliance and retained small-tile growth therefore do not suffice to establish attack-line quality or a deployable army advantage.

First visible hostile contact and the recorded latch agree:128 for tick,130 for fanout. Neither mode overrides afterward, even when the enemy disappears again. The independent checker confirms the latch and all priorities; this is not a contact-forgetting bug. Current attack plans remain protected after contact, although their state and opportunities differ from V10's original trajectory.

The opponent first sees our capital in its **original archived public wire** at238(tick),166(fanout),360(V10),288(V10-v6). This is retrospective diagnostic evidence from the opponent's view, never a feature supplied to our bot. Earlier exposure in fanout is observed, not established as the cause of its later attack. Neither V15 discovers the enemy general before losing. Construction is enabled but neither V15 builds before death; V10's seven builds occur much later, starting655.

## Complete terminal mechanisms

**Tick:** At225 the inherited parent sends half home24 west; that packet travels north and east, reaching21 at(6,14) on230. Enemy68 first appears on the final approach at(7,8) on229, then advances east/down along rows7/8. Our packet continues away through row4 while the enemy reaches48 at(8,16) on238. The defender memory is inactive and `intercept_feasible` remains false through the reported216–238 interval. A return from(7,17) boosts home to25 at238; the final(9,17) reinforcement is insufficient against the48 stack's attack. Terminal loss239 occurs despite84land/226army versus72/197 in the last observation: aggregate advantage is not arriving force.

**Fanout:** Enemy59 appears at(3,17) on356 and becomes62 at(4,17). At359 an actual interception begins, transferring6 from(16,17) toward home with projected arrival33 and new defense20 against required additional defense18. On360 the threat is temporarily outside our public view; the parent releases the commitment without expiry, observation-gap or ownership/army-inconsistency flags. It sends half home14 west instead. The enemy reappears with56 at(5,14) on363; no feasible interception is reported afterward. It reaches41 at(8,16) on368 versus home11, while the candidate issues remote row18 transfers. Loss369 is ordinary pre-deathtouch combat. The single start/release event is evidence of a specific lost defensive commitment, not a proven rescue opportunity or a broad oscillation claim.

A useful next discrimination is how precontact fanout affects transport to a useful front and capital exposure, followed by whether an existing defensive route should survive temporary threat fog. The data do not identify a safe replacement threshold. A retained frontier tile, a higher scoreboard army, and a legal reserve-preserving move are insufficient by themselves.

## Integrity and limitations

Frozen postcheck76226 exits0 on all4,022 original candidate frames. It verifies19/7/20/20 memory continuity, original raw and later-original-recorded control memory, every V15 proposal/count/argmax independently from public wires, contact/priority/window, actual parent/proposal attribution, legal1..3-army neutral capture and all eight cleared offensive fields. Last candidate-trajectory opponent invalid153(tick) and304(fanout), before the terminal intervals above. No errors were dropped or opponent actions repaired. This synchronous strategy arena has no official response deadlines; warm fixed-state profiling is separate evidence.

No new policy inference, game or hidden-state replay was used in analysis. Analysis96121 exited0 on its first attempt. All original/frozen hashes were rechecked. `analysis.json` retains every override, tick, terminal event and source binding; `postchecks.json` is the strict integrity audit; `delivery-manifest.json` records final release context and hashes without rewriting earlier complete reports.

## Economy, contact, and capital exposure

| Candidate placement | Public land/army at200, own vs enemy | First visible enemy | First enemy general seen | First own capital exposure in opponent wire |

The V10 control first exposes its capital at243 against Juraj and394 against my_bot9. Fanout therefore accompanies later observed exposure on Juraj but earlier exposure on my_bot9. Tick/my_bot9 exposure is later464 despite its loss. These measurements use the actual original opponent's public wire for audit only; that wire is never supplied to our policy. They do not establish that a particular frontier tile revealed the capital or that later exposure alone creates a winning strategy.

Fanout/Juraj temporarily improves land balance:59vs56 at200 and128vs119 at700, but is behind in total army at both observations181vs182 and530vs659. It builds its first castle only824; the opponent has no castles in this episode. Enemy capital remains undiscovered throughout. At800 its army608 trails770; more local land did not produce sufficient sustained offensive force or discovery.

Both my_bot9 candidate trajectories obtain a real early resource lead but fail to convert it. Tick reaches72land/244army vs30/141 at300, then loses the army lead by650(204vs211). It builds no castle; the opponent owns two by350 and retains two thereafter. Fanout reaches58land/248army vs40/172 at300, but by450 trails188vs224army. Its only build is381; the structure is later lost, and its subsequent one-castle ownership includes capture/recapture rather than another build. ## Terminal mechanisms

**Tick/Juraj:** identical to V10. Enemy43at(7,15) advances through(7,16),(8,16) then attacks home(8,17) at421. The final own reinforcement adds9 to home10, insufficient against moving38; normal capture ends422. No new frontier move is involved.

The candidate reports a47deficit and no feasible interceptor and moves a remote28→34field packet instead. Enemy47moving into home9 ends840 under deathtouch; its force is also larger than home defense. There is no enemy-general reveal, pursuit, or V10 mobilization anywhere in this episode. This is a late failure on the changed trajectory, not proof that any one of the retained opening tiles caused it.

**Tick/my_bot9:** after the sole action49, all remaining actions are V10 proposals. The bot finds the enemy general688 and issues52remembered-pursuit actions, but loses the defense/economic race. At800, enemy44at(14,8) advances west. Own26at(12,6) reinforces toward(14,6) over800/801; that screen reduces the invader to9 but does not stop it. At802 home28 half-attacks the adjacent enemy9 while that enemy sends8 into home. The smaller-source head-on attacker executes first and wins through deathtouch, ending803. The counterattack being individually sufficient does not make it win the simultaneous-order race.

**Fanout/my_bot9:** last frontier action59, no enemy-general discovery or mobilization. At601 enemy64at(14,8) reinforces(14,7) to65; at602 that65 sends64 into the already-owned adjacent30at(14,6), producing94. The candidate's14field packet marches home over601–603. The final reinforcement adds15 to home39, but enemy93moving exceeds54 and captures normally, ending604 before deathtouch. ## Interpretation and next discrimination

The narrow frontier contract executes correctly and earns retained income. It does not recover the winning V10-v6 Juraj behavior, and both candidate modes lose the selected my_bot9 placement won by both controls. Do not promote these modes from the proxy successes.

The evidence supports separating three questions in later work: net production per opening action rather than gross added-capture count; sustained usable attack force and capital discovery after first contact; and enemy production/merge-aware defense. A further neutral-action quota cannot be justified by these episodes. In particular, the my_bot9 leads demonstrate that gaining land early can coexist with losing the later production and attack race. Original lifecycle, raw histories, source bindings, and the strengthened strict checker passed on their first runs. next_direction_review:
# Next direction: measure an attack packet's completed work

The strongest next audit is a **paired complete-episode packet-progress and capture-retention audit of original V10 and V10-v6 on Amin case1 and Juraj V3.5 case12**. Their mirrors already have exact public/action/memory equivalence. Four representative original episodes, not another threshold wrapper, can distinguish useful reinforcement from repeated force redirection. No additional games or policy inference were performed for this design review.

## What the code actually optimizes

The inherited campaign is not a persistent capital-directed line. `sentinel_agent.py:118–133` selects a currently visible enemy general, otherwise an affordable neutral castle, otherwise **every passable visible enemy cell as a multi-source goal**, otherwise the farthest reachable fog frontier. With visible enemy land, distance therefore points toward a nearby enemy border, not an inferred enemy capital. At `154–163`, advancing scores `5 + 0.65 × moved`, capture adds local bonuses, and a friendly transfer must advance this newly computed goal field. This can create a useful feeder line and concentrate its largest moving force, but there is no persistent packet identity, previous strategic objective, capital-search hypothesis, information-gain budget, or concealment score. A changed border can change the direction that counts as progress.

V6 adds persistent **defender** transport; it does not add campaign memory. Its campaign remains the frozen score extraction (`sentinel_v6_agent.py:133`). V8 instead makes a persistent **one-enemy-cell concentration plan**. Its target score (`sentinel_v8_agent.py:81–100`) increases with enemy army, castle/general bonuses and a small home-distance penalty; the 7×7 donor pool is an initial availability filter. Only the highest-ranked target is then given owned-only attack routes and an assembly/deployment calculation. This is not a global comparison of feasible objectives, capital search, retained territory or opportunity cost. A better-ranked unreachable/expensive target can prevent considering a lower-ranked useful one; when no plan is issued, the parent still acts, so this is not an unconditional PASS deadlock.

V8's packet advances through owned cells to its selected enemy cell, checks continuity/force/expiry (`175–207`), and clears its offensive plan immediately on issuing the attack (`209–223`). It also releases if the objective ceases to be currently enemy-owned. It does **not** reserve a post-capture continuation, track retained gains, or continue a campaign to a strategic completion point. Repeated new objectives can therefore pull force toward locally valuable enemy armies instead of continuing an already useful front. This is an architectural mechanism, not proof that any particular retarget caused a recorded loss. The frozen V8 `expected_army` addition at221 is only retained for owned transfers: attack memory is cleared at223, so it is not a stale post-combat subtraction bug.

V9 remembers a previously seen stationary general, then scores current visible legal advances while that location is hidden (`sentinel_v9_agent.py:90–148`). It does not search for an unseen capital or retain a mobile enemy army. V10 wraps either V9 or V6 and mobilizes home after the competition threshold; comparing those two parents is therefore not a pure concentration factorial throughout every complete game. The recorded no-reveal preflight nevertheless proves unseen-general pursuit cannot explain the early Amin V10-v6 loss at370, before mobilization800.

## Why the existing evidence does not support one universal allocation rule

On Amin, V10's collections at129 and142 actually capture enemy tiles at132 and149. V10-v6 has more land at150 (72 versus64) but retains only6 of its next20 capture events through200, versus22 of28 for V10. The concentration trajectory wins1033; parent6 loses370. On Juraj, V10 spends31/33 owned transfers in100–149/150–199, with4/2 neutral attempts; parent6 spends22/29 transfers and17/5 neutral attempts and reaches67land at200 versus42. It eventually wins1075 while V10 loses422. These facts motivate comparing **which packet produces retained acquisitions and pressure**, rather than maximizing neutral count, minimizing all transfers, or rewarding assembly itself.

V14 repaid its service ledger but still lost both preservation cases. V15's actual opening overrides also fail: tick/fanout lose Amin239/369, Juraj422/840 and my_bot9 803/604. Tick makes no Juraj override at all, and the first original transfers already funded retained captures on18/19. Full opponent exposure diagnoses are still owned separately; these results alone do not prove that early visibility or capital leakage caused the losses. Both public views are available to measure what was actually revealed, while the policy must never receive the opponent's view.

## Three structural alternatives and the missing discrimination

1. **Persistent front packet and route progress.** Keep a packet after a successful capture, reconcile force through actual owned transfers/merges, and define a bounded meaningful destination or completion condition. Compare current route progress with redeployment cost before replacing its objective. This directly addresses the gap between one-tile V8 plans and a campaign. It must release for real defense, invalid ownership, insufficient force or changed terrain; an unconditional packet hold would merely create a new stall.
2. **Capital search with uncertainty and concealment.** Maintain a public-evidence search frontier or candidate region, reveal coverage, and a distinction between an attack corridor and incidental enemy land. Evaluate scouting routes with known terrain and explicit unknowns. Concealment requires a model of what an opponent could infer; 'we have not seen them' is not 'they have not seen us.' Current stationary-general memory is useful only after a sighting.
3. **Fog-retained defensive need.** V6 explicitly discards mobile-enemy locations between observations (`85–96`) and requires current visible need to retain a defender (`130`). A bounded last-seen threat envelope could prevent a screen from dissolving merely when the attacker goes out of sight, but uncertain force/route must not be fabricated as a current observation. Existing diagnosed terminal merges were visible and can fail for different route/force accounting reasons; fog persistence cannot be credited as their repair without a disappearance interval.

## One discriminating full-episode audit

Use the four completed original controls above, from turn0 through their real terminals. Retain all invalid replies and hash-bind both wires, joint actions, keys, memory, rules and frozen sources. Count both mirrors only as consistency checks. Produce:

- Every issued campaign/collection/deployment segment with actual source, destination, moving force and ownership after the joint step; link packet flow through merges and splits explicitly rather than inventing a unique identity when the evidence is ambiguous.
- Objective/route changes and release reasons available in archived telemetry, time spent assembling versus moving toward the same front, capture completion, then retention through the next tick and 50/100 further steps where the episode permits. Use right-censoring at terminal, not an invented failure for an unavailable future observation.
- Which friendly packet could physically reach the contested front/home on currently known routes, and where the originally issued action sends it. Record travel distance and deployable force separately from total scoreboard army; do not claim an alternative would defeat the adaptive opponent.
- First own contact, first opponent-visible candidate tile/general, first own enemy-general sighting, and actual intervening route coverage. Opponent visibility is a recorder-only diagnosis, never policy input. Compare full disclosure timelines, not just final general visibility.
- Every defense start/release with whether the threatening force remained visible, disappeared, merged, or changed route. A missing visibility interval distinguishes a fog-memory hypothesis from a visible-route certificate failure.

Evidence for packet persistence would be repeated fragmentation/retargeting before useful completion on Juraj, contrasted with sustained useful V10 delivery on Amin, while the lost packet was not needed for an earlier visible home deadline. Evidence for search would be available sustained force that instead revisits known enemy territory and delays new useful reveal. Evidence for fog defense would require a last-seen actionable threat followed by a release specifically during lost visibility. These are separate hypotheses; the same complete audit can reject explanations before another policy is built.

The current archives do not generically expose V6's rejected five-field proposal, all candidate targets, goal-field changes, or every failed gate. Do not reconstruct those as facts from `offense_override` alone. Exact on-record actions and memory support the first pass; a later separately authorized replay may recompute missing internal decisions on identical public inputs, with exact raw-action parity required first.

## Cost and evaluation limits

Persistent scalar packet/goal metadata alone is cheap, but a new search or threat-envelope planner may add convergent distance solves. Reuse one candidate-owned campaign context where practical; avoid calling the full V6/V8 solver for every hypothetical objective. Reusing stale fields after a simulated move is only a heuristic unless revalidated. No architecture above has a measured cost or a promised less-than-twofold overhead. Any candidate needs matched active/inactive CPU and batched-GPU timing, full-output synchronization, and separate cold/deployment cache qualification before strength evaluation.

This report proposes no source modification, inferred rescue, new match, or reserved143000 use. Competition construction/deathtouch evidence remains distinct from classic castle capture and FFA doctrine.
